title: Social life
about: Phrasal verbs and phrasal nouns for everyday social life: making plans, visiting people, going out and treating friends, arriving and leaving. Also how we talk about disappointments and getting over them.

items.pattern: get up to sth · with an object, not separable: What did you get up to? · informal · objects: what, much, nothing much, anything, something, mischief
items.meaning: do something, usually in your free time; about children it often means doing something naughty
items.example: So what did you **get up to** over the Easter holidays?
more: My grandparents are always **getting up to** something. Last month they tried paddleboarding.
I didn't **get up to** anything exciting on my day off. I mostly cleaned the flat.
items.watchOut: Не плутай з get up — вставати: What time did you get up? — коли ти встав? What did you get up to? — що ти робив? У питанні to стоїть у кінці. Це розмовне: у листі незнайомій людині краще What did you do?

items.pattern: treat sb / yourself to sth · with an object, the person goes straight after treat: treat Mum to a meal, treat her to it · preposition to, not with · objects: a meal, lunch, a night out, a trip, a present
items.meaning: pay for something nice for someone, or for yourself, as a present or a reward
items.uk: пригостити когось чимось; зробити приємне (і заплатити)
items.example: For their anniversary, the kids **treated** their parents **to** a boat trip on the lake.
more: I've had a terrible week, so I'm going to **treat** myself **to** a massage.
Put your purse away. I'm **treating** you **to** lunch today.
items.watchOut: Прийменник — to, не with: treat sb to dinner — пригостити вечерею. Treat sb with sth — лікувати чимось; treat sb with respect — ставитися до когось з повагою. «Я пригощаю» — It's my treat або It's on me.

items.pattern: take sb out (for a meal / to the cinema) · with an object, the person goes in the middle: take Mum out / take her out, never take out her · passive: be taken out
items.meaning: invite someone to go somewhere with you, such as a restaurant or the cinema, and usually pay
items.example: Dad **took** us **out** for pizza after the school concert.
more: He wants to **take** her **out** for dinner on her birthday.
When my cousin visits, I'll **take** him **out** to see the castle.
items.watchOut: Займенник посередині: take her out, не take out her. «Запросити в ресторан» — take sb out for a meal / for dinner. Take sth out — інше: дістати, винести (take the bins out). У військовому контексті take sb out — знищити, а провести до виходу — show sb out.

items.pattern: go on to a place · intransitive, followed by to + the next place · after somewhere else, often with then: then we went on to a club · written as two words: on to
items.meaning: go to a new place after the one you were at, as part of the same evening or trip
items.uk: піти далі (в інше місце), перебратися кудись ще
items.example: We had a drink at the hotel and then **went on to** a little fish restaurant by the harbour.
more: After the wedding, most of the guests **went on to** a party at the bride's house.
The match finished at nine, and some of the fans **went on to** a pub in the city centre.
items.watchOut: Go on to a place — після одного місця піти в наступне. Go on to do sth — згодом зробити щось (She went on to become a doctor). Go on doing sth — продовжувати те саме. Go out — піти розважатися, це інше.

items.pattern: pass by / pass by a place · intransitive or with a place, not separable: pass by the shop · often continuous: I was just passing by
items.meaning: go past a place or a person on your way somewhere else
items.example: I was **passing by** the bakery, so I bought us some croissants.
more: Wave to Grandma when we **pass by** her house.
Hundreds of tourists **pass by** our front door every day.
items.watchOut: Pass by — лише пройти чи проїхати повз. «Зайти в гості» так не скажеш: I was passing by, so I called in / dropped by. Не «I passed by you» у значенні «я зайшов до тебе».

items.pattern: call in on sb · with a person, not separable: call in on Grandma / call in on her · with a place: call in at the chemist's · mostly British
items.meaning: visit someone for a short time, usually on your way to another place
items.example: On the way back from the market, I **called in on** my aunt to see how her knee was.
more: Could you **call in at** the chemist's on your way home?
The nurse **calls in on** Mrs Hill every Friday to check she's all right.
items.watchOut: Call тут не «дзвонити»: call in on sb — заскочити до когось. До людини — on (call in on Grandma), до місця — at (call in at the bakery). Зателефонувати — просто call sb.

items.pattern: hang out (with sb) (at / in a place) · intransitive · informal · hang – hung – hung · noun: a hangout = a place where you often spend time
items.meaning: spend time with friends, or somewhere relaxed, without doing anything special
items.example: On Sundays we usually just **hang out** at Maria's and watch films.
more: Teenagers love to **hang out** in the shopping centre after school.
It was nice to **hang out** with my brother for a few days without any plans.
items.watchOut: Розмовне: у листі незнайомій людині — spend time with. Минулий час — hung out (hanged — лише «повісили людину»). Hang out the washing — розвішувати білизну, інше значення.

items.pattern: a (big / real / huge / bit of a) letdown · countable noun · be a letdown · from the verb let sb down · stress on let
items.meaning: something that turns out much worse than you hoped; a disappointment
items.example: After all the great reviews, the new Italian place was a real **letdown**.
more: The fireworks were a bit of a **letdown**. They were over in five minutes.
It was a huge **letdown** when our trip to the lakes was cancelled.
items.watchOut: Іменник пишеться разом (letdown, рідше let-down), наголос на першому складі: LETdown. Дієслово — let sb down: підвести когось (He let me down again).

items.pattern: drop by (a place) · intransitive or with a place: drop by / drop by the office, no to · informal · similar: drop in (on sb), call round, come by
items.meaning: visit someone for a short time, usually without arranging it first
items.example: My neighbour **dropped by** with a cake she'd baked.
more: **Drop by** any time you're in the area. I'm usually at home.
Can I **drop by** after work to pick up the drill?
items.watchOut: Drop тут не «впустити»: drop by — забігти ненадовго, часто без попередження. Місце ставлять одразу після by: drop by the office, без to.

items.pattern: move on (from sth) · intransitive · after a loss, a break-up, a failure · it's time to move on / I've moved on
items.meaning: stop thinking about something sad that has ended and get on with your life
items.example: It's been a year since the divorce, and she's finally ready to **move on**.
more: Some people find it hard to **move on** after losing a job.
They had a big argument, but they've both **moved on** now.
items.watchOut: Move on не означає «переїхати»: переїхати — move (house) або move away. «Жити далі» — не go further і не live further, а move on. Ще значення: перейти до наступного (Let's move on to the next question).

items.pattern: stand sb up · with an object, the person goes in the middle: stood me up / stood Kian up · passive: be stood up · informal · about a date or a meeting with a friend
items.meaning: not come to a date or a meeting you arranged, without telling the other person
items.uk: не прийти на побачення чи зустріч (і не попередити)
items.example: I waited outside the cinema for an hour. He'd **stood** me **up**.
more: Never **stand** someone **up**. At least send a message if you can't come.
I've been **stood up** twice by the same guy. Never again!
items.watchOut: Stand up — встати, а stand sb up — не прийти на зустріч з кимось. Займенник посередині: stood me up (не stood up me). Пасив: I was stood up — до мене не прийшли на побачення.

items.pattern: deal with sth / sb · with an object, not separable: deal with it, never deal it with · deal – dealt – dealt · objects: it, a loss, stress, change, bad news
items.meaning: accept a difficult situation or feeling and handle it
items.uk: впоратися з чимось, дати собі раду
items.example: Losing his job was hard, but he's **dealing with** it really well.
more: After the break-up she kept herself busy. That's how she **deals with** things.
Kids often **deal with** change better than adults do.
items.watchOut: Займенник після with: deal with it (не deal it with). Минулий час — dealt /delt/, не «дилд». Ще значення: займатися чимось, розбиратися (I'll deal with the bills).

items.pattern: a (small / family / informal) get-together · countable noun, with a hyphen · have / hold a get-together · verb: get together (with sb), no hyphen
items.meaning: an informal meeting of friends or family, often at someone's home
items.example: Mum's organising a little **get-together** for Dad's sixtieth on Sunday.
more: The school is holding a **get-together** for new parents before term starts.
Our old class has a **get-together** every five years.
items.watchOut: Іменник — з дефісом (a get-together), дієслово — без нього: Let's get together soon. Не називай таку зустріч a meeting: це звучить як ділова нарада.

items.pattern: hook up with sb · intransitive, with + the person, not separable · informal, mostly spoken · without with: Shall we hook up later?
items.meaning: meet someone so that you can do something together
items.example: I'm going to **hook up with** some old school friends while I'm back home.
more: I'm in London next week. Shall we **hook up** for a coffee?
Let's **hook up with** the others at the station and get the train together.
items.watchOut: Обережно: у сучасній розмовній мові, особливо американській, hook up with sb часто означає «мати випадковий секс». Щоб не було двозначності, кажи meet up with sb. Hook sth up — підключити (техніку).

items.pattern: shoot off (to a place) · intransitive · informal · shoot – shot – shot · I'd better shoot off / I have to shoot off
items.meaning: leave quickly, often because you have to be somewhere else
items.example: Sorry, I can't stay for coffee. I've got to **shoot off** to pick up the kids.
more: She always **shoots off** at five on the dot.
It's nearly ten. I'd better **shoot off** before the last bus goes.
items.watchOut: Розмовне. Минулий час — shot off. Нейтрально: I'd better go / I must be off. Shoot off підкреслює поспіх.

items.pattern: sleep sth off · with an object, separable: sleep off a hangover / sleep it off, never sleep off it · objects: a hangover, a big meal, a headache, a late night
items.meaning: sleep until you feel better, especially after eating or drinking too much
items.example: He had far too much wine at the wedding and spent Sunday **sleeping it off**.
more: I'm exhausted after the night flight. I'm going to **sleep it off**.
She went to bed early to **sleep off** her headache.
items.watchOut: Займенник посередині: sleep it off (не sleep off it). Не плутай з oversleep — проспати (і запізнитися) і sleep in — поспати довше вранці.

items.pattern: roll up (at / to a place) · intransitive · informal · subjects: guests, friends, crowds; often late or casually · similar: turn up, show up, rock up
items.meaning: arrive somewhere, often late or in a relaxed way
items.example: Half the guests **rolled up** an hour after the party had started.
more: Jack **rolled up** at the airport ten minutes before the gate closed.
Our friends always **roll up** late, so we tell them to come half an hour early.
items.watchOut: Розмовне. Як turn up / show up, але часто з відтінком «прийти пізно або неквапом». Roll up sth — скрутити, закасати (roll up your sleeves — закасати рукави), це інше.

items.pattern: turn sb away (from a place) · with an object, separable: turn away visitors / turn people away / turn them away, never turn away them · passive: be / get turned away
items.meaning: refuse to let someone go into a place, often because it is full
items.example: The museum was so busy that they were **turning** people **away** at the door.
more: The doctor's surgery had to **turn** patients **away** because so many staff were ill.
The shelter never **turns away** anyone who needs a bed for the night.
items.watchOut: Займенник посередині: turn them away (не turn away them). Без додатка turn away — відвернутися (She turned away and cried).

items.pattern: get into sth / doing sth · with an object, not separable: get into it · often with really / seriously · be into sth = already like it · informal
items.meaning: start to enjoy an activity and become more and more involved in it
items.example: My dad has really **got into** gardening since he retired.
more: I **got into** running a few years ago, and now I can't stop.
Once you **get into** the story, the book is hard to put down.
items.watchOut: «Захопився» — got into, а не got carried away (це «захопився й перестарався»). Get into ще означає «сісти, увійти» (get into a car) і «вступити» (get into university). Be into sth — уже подобатися: I'm into old films.

items.pattern: move away (from a place) (to a place) · intransitive · subjects: people, families · from a town, a village, an area
items.meaning: leave the area where you live and go to live somewhere else
items.example: When my best friend **moved away**, I felt really lonely for a while.
more: My sister **moved away** to Canada, so we mostly talk on video calls.
We **moved away** from the city when the kids were born.
items.watchOut: Move away — виїхати з міста чи району, move house — переїхати в інше житло, move out — виїхати з квартири (від батьків). Move on — інше: жити далі.

warmup.uk: Що ти робив, поки нас не було?
warmup.q: What did you ___ while we were away?
warmup.explain: Get up to sth — розмовне «робити, займатися». Get up — вставати з ліжка.
Пригостити чимось — treat sb to sth. Treat sb with sth — лікувати чимось.

warmup.uk: Дорогою додому я заскочив до бабусі.
warmup.q: On the way home I ___ Grandma.
warmup.explain: До людини — call in on sb, до місця — call in at (call in at the bakery).

warmup.uk: Минулого не повернеш. Треба відпустити й жити далі.
warmup.q: You can't bring back the past. You have to let go and ___.
warmup.explain: «Жити далі» — move on. Go further — пройти чи поїхати далі (про відстань).

warmup.uk: Він не прийшов до мене на побачення і навіть не написав.
warmup.q: He ___ and didn't even text me.
warmup.explain: Stand sb up — не прийти на зустріч. Займенник посередині: stood me up.

warmup.uk: Я так об'ївся, що мені треба відіспатися.
warmup.q: I've eaten so much that I need to ___.
warmup.explain: Відіспатися після переїдання чи вечірки — sleep it off. Oversleep — проспати.

warmup.uk: Нас не пустили до клубу, бо там було повно людей.
warmup.q: We were ___ from the club because it was packed.
warmup.explain: Не пустити — turn sb away. Turn off — вимкнути; put away — прибрати на місце.

warmup.uk: Останнім часом я дуже захопився йогою.
warmup.explain: Захопитися чимось — get into sth. Get in — увійти, сісти (в машину); get on — сісти (в автобус) або ладнати з кимось.

A.q: The concert was a real ___. The band only played for forty minutes.
A.explain: Letdown — розчарування. Let-off — коли вдалося уникнути покарання; breakdown — поломка або нервовий зрив.

A.q: My date ___ me up. I waited at the café for an hour, and he never came.
A.explain: Stand sb up — не прийти на побачення. Put sb up — пустити переночувати; get sb up — розбудити.

A.q: It's Mum's birthday next week, so we're going to ___ her out for lunch.
A.explain: Take sb out — повести кудись і заплатити.

B.q: Thanks for a lovely evening, but I must ___ off. I've got an early start tomorrow.
B.explain: Shoot off — розмовне «поспіхом піти». Sleep sth off — відіспатися; call sth off — скасувати.

B.q: Dozens of students ___ up at the café when they heard the coffee was free.
B.explain: Roll up — з'явитися, прийти (часто пізно чи неквапом). Hang up — покласти слухавку.

B.q: My sister has really ___ into running. She does a race every month now.
B.explain: Get into sth — захопитися. Go into — увійти або обрати професію; come into — успадкувати.

topics: a surprise visit from an old friend
a night out in the city
visiting relatives on the way to the seaside

example.title: Leo's surprise visit
example.uk:
Що я робив минулими вихідними? У п'ятницю без попередження заскочив мій давній друг Лео, і ми до півночі тусувалися в саду.

У суботу він пригостив мене обідом у новому тайському ресторані, який, чесно кажучи, трохи розчарував. Потім ми навідалися до моєї сестри, яка влаштувала невеликі посиденьки із сусідами. Лео нещодавно захопився сальсою, тож показав усім кілька кроків.

Пізніше ми пішли далі, до сальса-бару, але нас туди не пустили, бо Лео був у шльопанцях, тож ми до третьої ночі просиділи в караоке-барі. У неділю він відсипався до полудня, а потім помчав на свій потяг.
example.en:
What did I [[get up to|a1]] last weekend? On Friday my old friend Leo [[dropped by|a9]] without warning, and we [[hung out|a7]] in the garden until midnight.

On Saturday he [[treated me to|a2]] lunch at the new Thai place, which was a bit of a [[letdown|a8]], to be honest. Then we [[called in on|a6]] my sister, who was having a small [[get-together|b1]] with her neighbours. Leo has recently [[got into|b7]] salsa, so he showed everyone a few steps.

Later we [[went on to|a4]] a salsa bar, but they [[turned us away|b6]] because Leo was wearing flip-flops, so we ended up in a karaoke bar until three. On Sunday he [[slept it off|b4]] until noon and then [[shot off|b3]] to catch his train.
